sections.Kurzabstract: The German-language short version of the Depressions-Angst-Stress-Skalen (DASS) is used in pain research and treatment and was developed to capture core psychological aspects of depression, anxiety and stress. It comprises three scales with seven items each. The assessment of psychological distress is of central importance in pain research and treatment. For depression as a comorbidity of pain, there are particular methodological and conceptual difficulties. Reliability: Cronbach's alpha was alpha = .91 (depression), alpha = .78-.82 (anxiety) and alpha = .81-.89 (stress), respectively. Validity: Construct validity of the DASS was compared with the HADS (Hospital Anxiety and Depression Scale) and the ADS (Allgemeine Depressionsskala). Specificity and sensitivity for depression were determined using a structured clinical interview for DSM-IV (SKID) and were likewise compared with the ADS and HADS.
sections.Diagnostische Zielsetzung: The assessment of psychological distress is of central importance in pain research and treatment. For depression as a comorbidity of pain, there are particular methodological and conceptual difficulties. The psychometric properties of the German-language short version of the Depressions-Angst-Stress-Skalen (DASS) were examined. The instrument is used in pain research and treatment and was developed to solve specific confounding problems by avoiding somatic items and by focusing the questions on core psychological aspects of depression, anxiety and stress.
sections.Aufbau: The DASS comprises three scales with seven items each and four response options (0-3).
sections.Grundlagen und Konstruktion: The psychometric properties of the instrument were examined in patients with pain and in various samples without a primary pain problem (N = 950).
sections.Empirische Prüfung und Gütekriterien:
Reliability: Cronbach's α for the depression scale was at least α = .91; the values of the anxiety and stress scales for the revised version were between α = .78-.82 and α = .81-.89, respectively.
Validity: Construct validity of the DASS was compared with the HADS (Hospital Anxiety and Depression Scale) and the ADS (Allgemeine Depressionsskala). Specificity and sensitivity for depression were determined using a structured clinical interview for DSM-IV (SKID) and were likewise compared with the ADS and HADS.
Norms: No norm values are available. However, Nilges and Essau (2015) report means and the values of the 25th and 75th percentiles for different "Strichproben".
sections.Testkonzept/Theoretischer Hintergrund:
The development of the DASS (Depression-Anxiety-Stress-Scale), which first appeared in the English-speaking world and was translated into German and adapted by Nilges and Essau (2015; Depression-Angst-Stress-Skalen), is based on conceptual and methodological considerations. Lovibond and Lovibond (1995) concentrated on the core symptoms of depression and anxiety. The instrument serves to assess psychological distress. The aim was to avoid item overlap between depression and anxiety. To this end, in a first step, items were included that experts had selected as typical for anxiety or depression, respectively. These were grouped into three groups:
(1) Items clearly associated with anxiety but not with depression.
(2) Items clearly assigned to depression but not to anxiety.
(3) Items whose assignment to depression or anxiety could not be decided unambiguously.
sections.Testkonzept/Testaufbau:
The short version contains 21 questions with seven items each for the depression, anxiety and stress scales (see "Items" for the items and their scale membership). The questions refer to the past week, with the following response options:
0 = Traf gar nicht auf mich zu
1 = Traf bis zu einem gewissen Grad auf mich zu oder manchmal
2 = Traf in beträchtlichem Maße auf mich zu oder ziemlich oft
3 = Traf sehr stark auf mich zu oder die meiste Zeit.
sections.Testkonzept/Auswertungsmodus:
The scores (0-3) are summed separately to total scores for the 3 scales:
Depression: items 3+5+10+13+16+17+21
Anxiety: items 2+4+7+9+15+19+20
Stress: items 1+6+8+11+12+14+18.
The items are all keyed in the same direction, i.e. there is no reverse coding. From a cut-off value of 10 for the depression and stress scales and a value of 6 for the anxiety scale, an elevated level of these characteristics can be assumed.
sections.Testkonzept/Auswertungshilfen: For patients with pain symptoms, cut-off values are given from which an elevated level of the respective characteristic is likely to be present.
sections.Testkonzept/Auswertungszeit: Scoring takes 1 minute electronically and 2 minutes by hand.
sections.Durchführung/Testformen: The German adaptation exists as a short version with 21 items and as a long version with 42 items. The instrument has so far (as of 1/2021) been translated into 54 languages. All versions can be found on the following homepage: http://www2.psy.unsw.edu.au/dass.
sections.Durchführung/Altersbereiche: No restrictions are known; however, use from the age of 18 is suggested.
sections.Durchführung/Material: The questionnaire is available as a printed version or electronically.
sections.Durchführung/Instruktion:
The instruction is written and is read by the participants. Its wording is as follows:
„Fragen zu Ihrem Befinden
Bearbeitungshinweis: Bitte lesen Sie jede Aussage und kreuzen Sie die Zahl 0, 1, 2 oder 3 an, die angeben soll, wie sehr die Aussage während der letzten Woche auf Sie zutraf. Es gibt keine richtigen oder falschen Antworten. Versuchen Sie, sich spontan für eine Antwort zu entscheiden.
0 Traf gar nicht auf mich zu
1 Traf bis zu einem gewissen Grad auf mich zu oder manchmal
2 Traf in beträchtlichem Maße auf mich zu oder ziemlich oft
3 Traf sehr stark auf mich zu oder die meiste Zeit“
sections.Durchführung/Durchführungsvoraussetzunge: Interpretation by professional staff, as well as the participant's intellectual, motor and sensory prerequisites, should be sufficient for answering the questions.
sections.Testkonstruktion:
Test construction is based on classical test theory. The theoretical basis was provided by methodological considerations of Lovibond and Lovibond (1995), the developers of the English original. Factor-analytic results led to the formation of three factors or scales, which is reflected in the theory of Clark and Watson (1991). In 2015 the instrument was translated into German and psychometrically examined. The calculated item-total correlations and item difficulties are sufficient. The scale intercorrelations are high, as expected (see Table 2).

sections.Gütekriterien/Objektivität: Objectivity in administration, scoring and interpretation corresponds to that of a questionnaire with unambiguous completion and scoring algorithms.
sections.Gütekriterien/Reliabilität:
The internal consistency of the scales is Cronbach's alpha = .88 for the depression scale, alpha = .76 for the anxiety scale and alpha = .86 for stress. The lower limit for the item-total correlation of items is rit = .30. This value was not reached or fallen short of in any case.
The range between 10 % and 90 % was chosen as the limits for item difficulty, which corresponds to an item mean of 0.3 and 2.7, respectively. As was to be expected in a non-clinical sample (the participants were being treated for pain and not for depressive or anxiety disorders), clear floor effects are evident; the item means are low. For the depression scale, only item 21, at 0.29, falls below the 10 % limit,
3 items of the anxiety scale (4, 7 and 15) lie below this difficulty limit. The items of the stress scale all lie within the limits of 10 % and 90 %.
sections.Gütekriterien/Validität:
A confirmatory factor analysis confirmed the 3-factor structure. Construct validity and concurrent validity were demonstrated by comparisons with content-similar instruments for the scales depressivity and anxiety. These are the German version of the Hospital Anxiety and Depression Scale (HADS; Herrmann, Buss & Snaith, 1995), the Allgemeine Depressions-Skala (ADS; Hautzinger & Bailer, 1993), the Beck Depressionsinventar (BDI; Kammer, 1983) and the Beck Angstinventar (BAI; Margraf & Ehlers, 2002). In the validation study by Nilges and Essau (2015), the correlations were predominantly above r = .60.
Specificity and sensitivity for depression were determined using a structured clinical interview for DSM-IV (SKID; Wittchen, Zaudig & Fydrich, 1997) and were likewise compared with the ADS and HADS.
sections.Gütekriterien/Normierung:
No norms are available. Cut-off values were defined for the DASS, and means and standard deviations were calculated for four samples.

sections.Anwendungsmöglichkeiten:
Fields of application of the DASS include: screening instrument for depressivity, anxiety and stress specifically for persons with physical complaints.
They are also suitable for use in research, individual diagnostics and differential diagnostics.
sections.Bewertung: Although the depression scale contains only seven items, it is as reliable as the ADS with 21 items. Sensitivity and specificity in the classification of clinical cases are better than with the HADS. The DASS is a reliable and economical alternative to previous instruments for depression screening in pain patients, both in terms of time and cost (the instrument is free of licence fees). In addition, with the scale "körperliche Anspannung" (stress), an aspect that is of interest diagnostically and therapeutically, especially for patients with pain, and that has so far been little researched is captured.
